en.title: Shortest Prefix to Read to Form a Digit String
en.description:
For each query independently, read s sequentially from its beginning; extra characters may be discarded and the selected characters may be rearranged. Find the length of the shortest prefix that must be read to form the query; output −1 if it cannot be formed. The original text mistakenly called the return value a substring; the body text and examples make it clear that reading starts from the beginning, not from an arbitrary sliding window.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains the digit string s, the second line contains q, followed by q lines of length query; an empty query is written as 0 -. 1≤|s|≤100000, 1≤q≤20000, the total query length is 1..500000; characters are 0..9. The original text does not rule out occasional empty queries; this site supports them and returns 0.
en.output: First output q, then output q shortest prefix lengths.
en.explanation:
The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 3
7 10 -1; 4
0 1 2 -1; 2
3 -1. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Record the positions of each digit. If a query needs digit c r times, reading must reach at least the position of the r-th occurrence of c; the answer is the maximum of all these positions.
